LABEL: Phase 2A complete + Phase 2B trap distribution - granite4.1:3b, harness v2, 2026-09-05
hardware: Intel Core Ultra 5 225U, 12C/14T, 15.47 GB RAM, CPU inference
note_on_completion: First complete 30-task reference measurement in the project's history. Survived one session-tied kill at task 5 and resumed from the fsynced ledger using the recorded order seed.

PHASE_2A.STRADDLE_NOTE: The two figures land on OPPOSITE SIDES of the 25% band floor: raw 24.1% is below it, timing-clean 28.0% is above. The difference is entirely four tasks whose failure mode is a TIME limit measured with a clock the instrument itself flagged as untrustworthy. 2C branches on the RAW figure because it is the conservative one.
PHASE_2A.note_done_unannounced: ZERO. On the 8B this was the dominant failure mode - it wrote correct answers and never emitted <final>. The 3B terminates properly; its failures are wrong answers, not unannounced right ones. That is a clean behavioural difference between the two models.
PHASE_2A.note_on_H26: Flagged but NOT removed from the timing-clean denominator. max_steps is a STEP limit, which slow timing cannot manufacture; its wall clock is untrustworthy but its pass/fail is sound. Only the four budget_exhausted tasks are time-limit failures.

machine_faults.M11: stalled three times across two runs (timeout at 152 tokens; 1.17 tok/s vs 5.63 median; timeout at 0 tokens) -> EXCLUDED
machine_faults.H23: stalled once at 0.17 tok/s vs 5.89 median (147 tokens in 850 s, a 35x slowdown) -> re-ran and completed as plateau. Its result is valid and measured.
machine_faults.note: Stalls are TASK-CONCENTRATED, not random. Across the session they land on M11, H23, H30, E02 and E06 repeatedly while H25 ran clean three times and E01 five. Both offenders here are medium/hard with long generations, which is a lead for DEFERRED D2 where the cause is still unknown.

worker_refreshes.note: Condition-dependent, NOT a fixed per-task overhead. The earlier aborted run fired on every task; this run fired 6 times in 30. The ~14 s/task estimate was wrong as a general figure - 87.9 s total is 0.7% of the run.

classified.family: wrong body: earth mu, not moon

PHASE_2B.acceptance_guard: HELD. Of the five no-trap tasks, E06/H25/M19 passed and are not in the failure set; H24 returned no_artifact; M18 returned unclassifiable. None force-fitted.
PHASE_2B.VERDICT: B/A = 10.5% strict, 15.8% inclusive. Both far below the 50% branch threshold. STOP.
PHASE_2B.WHAT_THE_FAILURES_ACTUALLY_LOOK_LIKE: Overwhelmingly unstructured rather than trap-shaped. Written values include 4.3e10 (M22), 5.3e12 (M21), 5.2e-23 (M13), 9.7e-04 (E08), 2.4e-03 (E02), 0.0 (M16), and NEGATIVE numbers on H28 (-19115.85), H23 (-2038.86) and M17 (-779.93). A negative escape velocity or delta-v is not a units confusion or a wrong-body error - it is a program that ran and never implemented the physics. This reproduces the original bucket-D taxonomy (14 of 15 unstructured, median relative error 100%) on the FIXED harness, which is the important part: the plumbing defects that explained the first 10% are gone, and the failures are still unstructured.
PHASE_2B.ONE_STRUCTURED_FAILURE_NOT_COUNTED: E04 wrote 4913.26 against 4233.9. Decomposing by hand: 4913.26/(311*9.80665) = 1.6110, so ln(mass ratio) = 1.6110 and the ratio used was 5.008 = (549054+137000)/137000. The model ADDED the masses instead of using m0 directly. That is a real, identifiable mistake - but it is not the trap E04 declares ('Isp in seconds needs g0') and it is not in any declared family, so the decomposer correctly returns unclassifiable rather than inventing a category. Worth recording because it shows 'unclassifiable' is not the same as 'random'.

DECOMPOSER_DEFECTS_FOUND_AND_FIXED_DURIN.defect: ZeroDivisionError on a written value of 0.0
DECOMPOSER_DEFECTS_FOUND_AND_FIXED_DURIN.detail: M16 wrote v_apogee_m_s: 0.0 and the residual divided by abs(got). A written zero is a real outcome - the original bucket D recorded two of them - and it crashed the instrument outright.
DECOMPOSER_DEFECTS_FOUND_AND_FIXED_DURIN.fix: scale the residual by |expected| when the written value is zero

DECOMPOSER_DEFECTS_FOUND_AND_FIXED_DURIN.defect: TypeError on a non-numeric expected value
DECOMPOSER_DEFECTS_FOUND_AND_FIXED_DURIN.detail: H27 expects bad_row_indices = [12, 21, 30, 34]. It is an anomaly-detection task, structurally outside a numeric decomposer's scope. Reported as its own category rather than forced.
DECOMPOSER_DEFECTS_FOUND_AND_FIXED_DURIN.fix: detect non-numeric expected and report non_numeric

DECOMPOSER_DEFECTS_FOUND_AND_FIXED_DURIN.defect: The residual gate was BELOW the rounding floor of its own inputs, for the second time
DECOMPOSER_DEFECTS_FOUND_AND_FIXED_DURIN.detail: 2e-5 was derived from E03's floor of 9.4e-06. But the floor varies per task with how precisely the suite tabled the value: E07's isp_s is 287.7, whose floor is ~1.7e-04. E07's written 2821.7522658610274 is EXACTLY thrust/mdot = Isp-without-g0, matching the declared trap at residual 1.34e-04 - and was reported unclassifiable because of the tolerance rather than the data.
DECOMPOSER_DEFECTS_FOUND_AND_FIXED_DURIN.fix: per-task tolerance = 3 half-ulps, measured in SIGNIFICANT FIGURES not decimal places, because the suite writes some values as 7.138e6 which repr renders as 7138000.0 and a decimal count would read as far more precise than it is

DECOMPOSER_DEFECTS_FOUND_AND_FIXED_DURIN.defect: Body swaps never crossed with radius formation
DECOMPOSER_DEFECTS_FOUND_AND_FIXED_DURIN.detail: E10 wrote sqrt(mu_earth/R_earth) - Earth's constants AND the altitude dropped. Candidates only ever applied the altitude to the swapped body, so the compound could not be generated. A model that gets the body wrong is exactly the one likely to mishandle the altitude too.
DECOMPOSER_DEFECTS_FOUND_AND_FIXED_DURIN.fix: generate body-swap x {altitude correct, ignored, km-read-as-m}

note_on_those_fixes: All four were found by decomposing values rather than trusting the tool's verdict, and all four moved B UPWARD (1 -> 3). The conclusion did not change - 15.8% is still far below 50% - but it would have been reported as 5.3% on a tool defect. The instruction to verify before branching to STOP was load-bearing.
